column5: OS booklet: maps have a key; OS maps are printed with north at the top; compass-point rhymes; National Grid of 100 km squares named by two letters; eastings first ('along the corridor, then up the stairs'); four-figure squares and six-figure points; 1:25,000 is 4 cm to 1 km with 1 km grid squares; string along the route against the scale bar; 10 cm of string is 2.5 km; most people walk at 3 km an hour. Matches module 5 throughout.

OS booklet: crossing a 1 km grid square diagonally is about 1.5 km, and at 3 km an hour a straight crossing takes about 20 minutes. The course says 'a little more than 1 km (our inference)'; replace with the OS figure.

OS booklet contours: brown contour lines join points of equal height above sea level; at 1:25,000 the vertical interval is usually 5 metres, or 10 metres in mountainous areas; lines close together mean a steep slope, far apart a gentle one; think of them as tide marks left every 5 metres. Module 5 does not teach contours yet, though they decide the effort and the pitch.

OS booklet: when giving a position, add a nearby landmark or feature to the six-figure reference for extra accuracy (for example, at the crossroads). Supports the rescue-call tip in module 5 and the call script in module 6.
